subject: Week to 25 October: what changed in reviews, and why it might have
recipients: GM, Operations, Area managers, Marketing, Product · store managers get their own section · internal only
lead: Most of this week's change sits in two places: stale donuts after 8 pm at three south-east Melbourne stores, and longer waits at food-court stores while the half-dozen deal ran. One allergen review was escalated on Saturday. Every insight below comes with its evidence, and every suggestion is only a suggestion: comment on any of them.

findings.headline: What did customers write about most this week?
findings.premise: Freshness and service were the themes customers mentioned most across the whole network, as they have been for the last 3 months. Mentions of waiting grew, and almost all of that growth came from food-court stores.

number.label: % of mentions were about waiting, up from 11% over the last 3 months

findings.status: Theme shares counted by code from 412 coded reviews; no explanation claimed.

evidence.detail: 371 reviews posted 19–25 October, each coded by theme with a quote
41 rated orders with written comments from Uber Eats, DoorDash and Menulog

findings.headline: Why did complaints about stale donuts jump after 8 pm at three south-east Melbourne stores?
findings.premise: Reviews calling the donuts stale rose at Stores 12, 14 and 17 this week, and most describe an evening visit. The rise coincides with those stores keeping a full display after 8 pm since their closing time moved later on 5 October.

number.label: reviews mentioning stale donuts after 8 pm, against an average of 6 a week over the last 3 months

findings.status: Coincides with the later closing time and full evening displays at all three stores. Not yet tested.
findings.suggestion: Suggestion: at one of the three stores, trial a smaller final bake and a reduced display after 8 pm for two weeks, then compare its stale mentions and waste with the other two.

evidence.detail: 23 reviews at Stores 12, 14 and 17 mention stale donuts and an evening visit
sales after 8 pm make up 9% of the day at all three stores
end-of-day waste has risen at all three stores since 5 October

findings.headline: What is one new store manager doing that customers keep praising?
findings.premise: Since a new manager started at Store 31 · western Melbourne on 14 September, reviews praising quick, friendly service have risen, and many name the manager. Staff names stay with the area manager and never feed performance reviews.

number.label: reviews this week praise the service, against 5 a week before the manager started

findings.status: Consistent with the manager change; the other western Melbourne stores show no rise.
findings.suggestion: Suggestion: ask the manager what changed at the counter, and turn it into a short training note for other stores.

evidence.detail: 14 reviews praise the service; 9 of them name the manager
new manager from 14 September; no other roster change

findings.headline: Did the weekday half-dozen deal bring in buyers but slow the food-court counters?
findings.premise: The deal sold well at food-court stores, and wait-time complaints at those stores rose in the same lunch hours. Food-court stores were already serving the most transactions per staff hour. The promotions calendar takes the deal to petrol-station kiosks from 2 November.

number.label: wait-time complaints at Stores 14, 22 and 26 this week, against 11 in the week before the deal

findings.status: Coincides with the deal's lunch-hour redemptions; rosters were not changed for the deal.
findings.suggestion: Suggestion: before the deal reaches the kiosks, add one staff hour over lunch at food-court stores, or start the deal at 2 pm, and compare waits.

evidence.detail: weekday half-dozen deal ran 19–25 October at all stores; kiosks join from 2 November
food-court redemptions peaked between 12 and 2 pm
no extra lunch hours rostered at Stores 14, 22 and 26
32 wait-time complaints at the three food-court stores

findings.headline: Why are kiosk customers buying fewer items per sale when their reviews barely changed?
findings.premise: Items per sale at petrol-station kiosks have fallen for four weeks, with no matching change in reviews. Stock records show the glazed range selling out before noon on most days, so customers may be leaving with less than they came for.

number.label: items per sale at petrol-station kiosks this week, against 2.2 over the last 3 months

findings.status: Consistent with morning stock-outs of the glazed range. Other explanations not yet ruled out.
findings.suggestion: Suggestion: move one tray of glazed stock onto the morning delivery at Stores 8 and 29 for two weeks, and compare items per sale.

evidence.detail: items per sale has fallen each week since 28 September
glazed range sold out before noon on 5 of 7 days

findings.headline: Was a customer told a donut was nut-free before an allergic reaction?
findings.premise: One Google review posted on Saturday at Store 22 · western Melbourne describes an allergic reaction after a donut the customer says staff called nut-free. The desk doesn't judge the claim. It sent the review to the area manager and the food-safety lead as soon as it was coded.

number.label: review, escalated on the day it was posted

findings.status: Escalated; the food-safety lead's review is open.
findings.suggestion: Suggestion: hold any public reply until the food-safety lead has reviewed it.
findings.escalated: Saturday 25 October, 3:40 pm, to the area manager and the food-safety lead

findings.headline: Which stores went quiet this week: fewer customers, or just fewer reviews?
findings.premise: Stores 3 and 8 each got too few reviews this week for the desk to report their themes, so they are left out of the theme shares. Sales at the regional kiosk also fell, while the Geelong store held steady.

number.label: reviews each at Stores 3 and 8, below the minimum of 10 a week the desk needs to report a store's themes

findings.status: Below the minimum sample; no themes reported for these stores.
findings.suggestion: Suggestion: put a QR survey card on the counter at both stores for two weeks, to show whether customers are quieter or simply fewer.

evidence.detail: transactions against the 3-month average: Store 8 · regional Victoria and the border down 12%, Store 3 · Geelong region within 2%

store_sections.note: Stale mentions after 8 pm are the main change this week, and the weekly rating sits below its 3-month baseline.
One allergen review was escalated on Saturday. Wait-time complaints also rose while the lunch deal ran.
Service praise is still rising. The area manager has the detail behind it.
Too few reviews this week to report themes. Thursday's 34°C heat coincides with two reviews about melted glaze.

meeting.note: The desk keeps this week's session open for Thursday's ops meeting. Ask it a question there and it answers from the same evidence, or tests two explanations side by side.
questions: Should one south-east Melbourne store trial a smaller evening bake?
Should the half-dozen deal wait for extra lunch staff before it reaches the kiosks?
Who follows up the allergen review, and when?
